requirements.title: Persistent projects and project settings
requirements.statement: The application shall create, name, reopen, duplicate, and persist editing projects, including their media references, timeline, output settings, and revisions.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new project opens an empty collection and timeline without requiring an AI account.
After saving and restarting the application, timeline content, output settings, selected profiles, and project metadata are unchanged.
Project duplication produces an independent edit history while safely reusing immutable source media.
Project deletion clearly distinguishes deleting editing data from deleting original media; originals are not deleted by default.

requirements.title: Collection-based batch ingestion
requirements.statement: The collection shall accept batches of video, audio, and image files, including large camera recordings, with visible import progress and recoverable failures.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can add multiple files through a file picker and drag-and-drop, then see per-file queued, importing, ready, or failed states.
An interrupted large upload can resume or retry without duplicating the media asset or exhausting server memory.
A failed or unsupported file does not prevent valid files in the same batch from importing.
Local file references, when offered, are limited to explicitly configured import roots; browser filenames are never treated as trusted server paths.

requirements.title: Immutable originals and stable asset identities
requirements.statement: Each imported asset shall have a stable identifier and provenance, and editing shall never modify the original media bytes.

acceptance_criteria.text: Checksums before and after trim, synchronization, grading, subtitle generation, and export match for every original.
Re-importing the same bytes identifies an existing asset or deliberately creates another reference without silent storage duplication.
Timeline references survive filename changes and supported relinking without silently substituting different content.
Derived proxies, thumbnails, transcripts, and renders record their source asset, source revision or checksum, and generation settings.

requirements.title: Media probing, exact dimensions, and source timing
requirements.statement: Ingestion shall probe actual video and audio stream properties rather than infer resolution, frame rate, or camera capabilities from names.

acceptance_criteria.text: Persist actual width and height, sample/display aspect ratio, rotation, duration, time base, frame-rate metadata, codec, pixel format, color tags, and audio stream properties when available.
Distinguish 60/1 from 60000/1001 and inspect presentation timestamps when constant versus variable frame rate is uncertain.
Accept a real or synthetic approximately 2K, 60 fps input; display its exact pixel dimensions instead of treating the label 2K as a specification.
Handle multiple audio streams, no audio, portrait rotation metadata, and missing optional tags without inventing values.

requirements.title: Capture date, timezone, and location metadata
requirements.statement: The application shall extract available capture date, time, timezone, location, and camera metadata, preserve provenance, and support user corrections.

acceptance_criteria.text: Show raw metadata and normalized values separately, including whether capture time and timezone are known, assumed, or user-supplied.
Do not equate file modification time with recording time or silently treat timezone-free camera timestamps as UTC.
Missing GPS or location remains unknown; manual city and timezone labels are supported and retained.
An optional reverse-geocoding request requires consent before coordinates leave the system, and exported metadata can omit location.

requirements.title: Library organization and filtering
requirements.statement: The collection shall support stable labels and filters for camera or perspective, recording day, location, pairing, duration, and analysis status.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can tag or correct camera A/B, left/right preference, trip day, and city in bulk or per asset.
Sorting by capture time respects declared timezone handling and exposes unknown or conflicting timestamps.
Users can preview and select assets using combinations of text, date, location, camera, and analysis filters.
Changing a label updates suggestions without silently rewriting existing manual timeline edits.

requirements.title: Proxies, thumbnails, and waveforms
requirements.statement: The system shall generate bounded, cacheable preview proxies, thumbnails, and audio waveforms while preserving exact links to original source time.

acceptance_criteria.text: Proxy generation is a visible asynchronous job and can be cancelled or retried.
Preview proxies preserve duration, orientation, aspect ratio, and a mapping to original presentation timestamps, including variable-rate inputs.
Final exports use originals unless the user explicitly selects a clearly labeled draft/proxy export.
Derived caches can be evicted and regenerated without losing edits, source files, or synchronization anchors.

requirements.title: Reviewable accidental-recording detection
requirements.statement: The system shall flag likely accidental or unusable recordings as reviewable suggestions, never delete or discard them irreversibly.

acceptance_criteria.text: At minimum inspect decode failure, unusually short duration, prolonged near-black imagery, frozen frames, and silence, with configurable thresholds and reasons.
A silent scenic shot and a dark but usable night scene remain available; absence of speech is not proof of no content.
Users can include or exclude flagged clips and override the classification; overrides survive reanalysis.
AI draft generation reports which assets were excluded and why, and can restore them into another proposal.

requirements.title: Broken media and relinking
requirements.statement: Missing, corrupted, unsupported, or inaccessible media shall produce recoverable errors rather than fabricated successful analysis or export.

acceptance_criteria.text: The collection and affected timeline items display the specific problem and retain their edit metadata.
Relinking validates identity or asks for explicit replacement confirmation when the content differs.
Exports using broken media fail preflight or require an explicit, recorded gap policy; they never silently omit clips.
Errors identify the failing asset and actionable diagnostics without exposing secrets.

requirements.title: Portable project backups
requirements.statement: Users shall be able to export and restore a versioned editing-project bundle, with optional original media inclusion and a manifest of external references.

acceptance_criteria.text: A metadata-only bundle restores projects after media relinking; a self-contained bundle restores without external paths.
Bundles contain edit decisions, profiles, sections, subtitles, and provenance but never API keys or session credentials.
Import validates bundle paths, schema version, hashes, and reference integrity before modifying an existing project.
Unsupported future schema versions are rejected safely and existing projects remain unchanged.

requirements.title: Non-destructive multitrack timeline
requirements.statement: The editor shall provide multiple simultaneous video, audio, image, and text tracks with non-destructive clip instances.

acceptance_criteria.text: A project can contain at least four simultaneous video tracks, four audio tracks, and independent overlay tracks; this is a baseline test, not an artificial product limit.
Each clip instance has independent source in/out, timeline position, track, transform, and relevant audio or effect settings.
Layer order, track visibility, mute, solo, and lock have defined, consistent effects in preview and export.
Using the same asset twice creates independent clip instances rather than altering the source or the other instance.

requirements.title: Canonical rational timing and temporal invariants
requirements.statement: All editing, synchronization, subtitles, and rendering shall share a canonical timing model with exact rational values or integer ticks and explicit time domains.

acceptance_criteria.text: Distinguish source presentation time, synchronization-group time, project time, section time, and export time.
Use half-open intervals [start, end) and reject negative durations, invalid source bounds, NaN values, and unsupported time transforms.
At 60000/1001 fps, repeated edits and long timelines do not accumulate errors from rounding the rate to 60 or storing frame counts as approximate seconds.
Variable-frame-rate inputs are mapped by presentation timestamps; output frame-rate conversion does not change intended playback speed.

requirements.title: Manual editing and precision controls
requirements.statement: Users shall be able to manually drag, arrange, trim, split, extend within available handles, and delete clip instances using familiar timeline interactions.

acceptance_criteria.text: Dragging either clip edge changes its visible interval with snapping and precise numeric in/out controls.
Split-at-playhead, move, reorder, insert, overwrite, and ripple-delete have documented effects on linked items and downstream material.
Users can zoom and scroll the timeline, select a range, step frames, and navigate with keyboard controls.
Invalid trims beyond source handles are prevented or require an explicit freeze/gap effect; the editor never invents source frames.

requirements.title: Basic transitions and handles
requirements.statement: The editor shall support hard cuts, video cross-dissolves, fades to or from a background, and audio fades or crossfades with editable timing.

acceptance_criteria.text: Transition start, end, and duration can be adjusted through the timeline and the editing API.
The editor validates available source handles and prevents accidental shortening, overlap corruption, or audio duplication.
Transitions between split-screen and full-width segments render consistently without leaving stale imagery from a previous layout.
Shortening or deleting a transition is undoable and updates dependent subtitle and section timing correctly when project time changes.

requirements.title: Undo, redo, autosave, and revisions
requirements.statement: All user and AI editing mutations shall be versioned, undoable, and recoverable after interruption.

acceptance_criteria.text: A multi-operation AI edit can be undone as one transaction and redone without changing unrelated edits.
Autosave does not mark an edit durable until its atomic persistence succeeds; restart recovers the last durable revision.
History records actor, timestamp, affected objects, previous revision, and a human-readable change summary.
An export is pinned to one immutable revision even while the user continues editing.

requirements.title: Concurrent user and AI edit safety
requirements.statement: An AI proposal shall not overwrite newer user changes or locked timeline objects without an explicit resolution policy.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every proposal references the project revision it read and the assets or objects it intends to change.
A proposal based on a stale revision is rejected with a structured conflict, safely rebased with renewed validation, or presented for user resolution.
Locked objects are protected by the domain service, not only by UI controls.
Users can scope a prompt to selected clips or sections; edits outside the scope are rejected unless explicitly authorized.

requirements.title: Usable synchronized preview
requirements.statement: The editor shall provide a preview canvas with play/pause, scrubbing, frame stepping, timeline selection, audio playback, and visible render status.

acceptance_criteria.text: Preview presents all visible layers and the selected final audio routing, not one independent audio player per camera.
Proxy-backed playback and quality changes do not modify project frame rate, timing, or export quality.
The current playhead, clip selection, trim handles, waveforms, and overlay selection remain coordinated.
Scrubbing or frame inspection uses bounded work and displays pending reference frames rather than blocking the entire interface.

requirements.title: Configurable canvas, dimensions, and output rate
requirements.statement: Projects and export presets shall define output aspect ratio, exact pixel dimensions, and frame rate independently of individual inputs.

acceptance_criteria.text: The initial canvas defaults to 16:9 and 1920x1080; 1:1, 9:16, and validated custom dimensions are selectable.
An Auto frame-rate setting resolves from the selected reference or dominant source on first draft; 60/1 input remains 60/1 and 60000/1001 remains distinct.
If no source exists, display a provisional 30 fps default; once resolved, do not silently change project timing after another import.
Validate encoder constraints such as even dimensions and explain any requested adjustment rather than silently stretching media.

requirements.title: Aspect-preserving composition and transforms
requirements.statement: Clip instances shall support position, scale, crop, rotation, opacity, z-order, and explicit contain or cover fitting inside layout regions.

acceptance_criteria.text: Contain preserves the complete source image with an explicit background; cover fills the region with visible crop controls.
No default operation stretches a source to change its aspect ratio.
Users and AI can specify transforms in normalized canvas or region coordinates, with preview and export using the same semantics.
Per-clip focal position or crop can be set manually or as a static AI suggestion; this does not require object tracking.

requirements.title: Two-perspective split-screen layout
requirements.statement: The editor shall provide a reusable left/right split-screen layout for synchronized sources of arbitrary aspect ratios.

acceptance_criteria.text: For a 1920x1080 canvas and two square sources in contain mode, each image is 960x960 with 60 pixels of vertical background above and below; sources remain undistorted.
Cover mode fills each 960x1080 region by cropping; the user can inspect and adjust the crop rather than accepting hidden loss of content.
Users can swap perspectives, resize the divider, configure a gap or background, and save a layout preset.
The layout binds clip instances and synchronization-group membership without changing the selected final audio source.

requirements.title: Mixed split-screen and full-width segments
requirements.statement: A sequence shall switch between simultaneous split-screen recordings and single full-width recordings, then return to split-screen without creating separate projects.

acceptance_criteria.text: A split/full/split fixture displays both perspectives, then the full 16:9 shot, then both perspectives again at the specified boundaries.
The full-width segment can use its own audio while adjacent split segments use their designated reference audio.
Cuts and transitions retain the intended total duration, synchronization, and subtitle mapping.
Users and AI can change the layout per segment rather than only globally.

requirements.title: Preview and export composition parity
requirements.statement: Preview and final rendering shall derive from the same validated composition model and share testable rendering semantics.

acceptance_criteria.text: Compare reference frames around cuts, overlays, crops, subtitles, grades, and layout transitions against the final encoded result.
Any browser approximation is explicitly labeled and a backend reference-frame preview is available for authoritative inspection.
Define numerical or image-mask tolerances suitable for lossy codecs rather than requiring byte-identical GPU and CPU outputs.
No effect is advertised as supported in final export solely because it appears in the browser preview.

requirements.title: Synchronization candidate matching
requirements.statement: The system shall propose likely simultaneous recordings and camera pairs using available capture metadata, audio similarity, and user camera labels.

acceptance_criteria.text: Display candidate pairings, evidence, estimated overlap, and confidence; the user can override or create a group manually.
Do not pair unrelated recordings merely because filenames or coarse timestamps are similar.
Handle different start and end times and recording segments split into multiple files without assuming one-to-one filenames.
Retain the pairing decision independently from layout and final audio routing.

requirements.title: Audio-based offset estimation
requirements.statement: When recordings contain sufficiently correlated audio, the system shall estimate their temporal offset from the original audio signals.

acceptance_criteria.text: Use audio from a camera for synchronization even when that camera will be muted in the final edit.
Test positive and negative known offsets, gain changes, background noise, different audio sample rates, and partial overlaps.
Report the estimation method, residual error or equivalent confidence evidence, and aligned source intervals.
On the qualified synthetic fixtures in AT-04, alignment error is at most one project output frame; do not generalize this bound to arbitrary real footage.

requirements.title: Silent or weak-evidence synchronization
requirements.statement: For sources without usable shared audio, the system shall attempt available timestamp or explicit visual-event alignment and otherwise offer manual anchors.

acceptance_criteria.text: A visible shared flash or marked event may establish an offset; object tracking is not required.
Coarse camera timestamps alone are labeled approximate, especially when clocks or timezones differ.
When neither shared audio, reliable timestamps, nor a common event exists, return insufficient evidence rather than a fabricated exact alignment.
A manual anchor can complete synchronization without requiring the silent source to gain an audio track.

requirements.title: Persistent synchronization transforms
requirements.statement: Persist synchronization as explicit reversible transforms between each source time domain and a chosen group reference.

acceptance_criteria.text: Document the offset sign convention and store source anchors, method, confidence, and residuals.
The same real-world event maps to the same group time across sources, including sources that began earlier or later.
Changing the selected reference re-expresses transforms without altering established relative alignment.
Synchronization never overwrites or physically trims source files.

requirements.title: Unequal coverage and missing-perspective policy
requirements.statement: The editor shall explicitly handle unequal recording coverage rather than repeat stale frames or silently discard material.

acceptance_criteria.text: Default auto-draft split-screen segments use the common overlap and preserve unused material in the collection.
Users may instead retain the union using an explicit full-width fallback, background gap, or separately selected freeze policy.
For A covering master time 0..30 and B covering 2..27, default split coverage is 2..27, not 0..30.
The UI shows which time spans lose a perspective or reference audio and explains the selected policy.

requirements.title: Clock-drift detection and correction
requirements.statement: The synchronization subsystem shall inspect alignment at multiple points, identify evidence of clock drift, and support a recorded affine time correction when justified.

acceptance_criteria.text: Distinguish a constant offset from progressive drift using more than one anchor on a sufficiently long recording.
A qualified synthetic offset-plus-drift fixture aligns at beginning, middle, and end to within one output frame after correction.
Apply the chosen mapping consistently to video, audio, and transcript times; preserve audio pitch when time-stretching audio.
Low-confidence or non-linear drift is flagged for manual review; a single uncertain match is not silently converted into a speed change.

requirements.title: Linked edits preserve synchronization
requirements.statement: Timeline edits on a synchronized group shall preserve relative timing unless the user explicitly chooses to slip or unlink one source.

acceptance_criteria.text: Moving, splitting, ripple-deleting, or trimming a linked group updates all affected video, audio, and overlay mappings as specified.
A deliberate single-source slip warns that alignment changes and creates an undoable operation.
Locked linked members prevent a conflicting group edit rather than leaving the group partially updated.
Undo and redo restore both visible arrangement and synchronization transforms.

requirements.title: Manual synchronization tools
requirements.statement: Users shall be able to inspect and refine synchronization using waveform views, reference-frame comparisons, anchors, and precise nudges.

acceptance_criteria.text: Provide one-frame video nudges and numeric offsets with finer audio precision where supported.
Allow setting at least two corresponding event anchors for drift inspection or correction.
Play an aligned preview with one reference audio source and expose the predicted residual or manual status.
Manual overrides remain stable during subsequent automatic draft or analysis operations unless explicitly reset.

requirements.title: Explicit master audio and routing
requirements.statement: A segment or synchronization group shall be able to use one selected source audio track as the final audio while displaying multiple video perspectives.

acceptance_criteria.text: Selecting camera A as reference audio mutes camera B in the final mix without removing B audio needed for analysis.
A silent secondary video is supported without generating a synthetic duplicate audio stream.
Switching between split-screen and full-width segments follows explicit segment-level audio routing and fade rules.
An unavailable reference audio stream triggers a visible fallback decision, not an unnoticed substitute.

requirements.title: Independent audio tracks and basic mixing
requirements.statement: The timeline shall support independent audio clips and basic mixing controls for source audio, voice, music, and other imported audio.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can add audio-only assets, trim and move them, adjust gain, mute or solo, and apply fades or crossfades.
Provide level metering and clipping warnings; optional loudness normalization remains an explicit, reversible choice.
Audio sample-rate conversion and encoder delay handling do not introduce a growing video/audio offset.
Unselected camera audio is not accidentally doubled into the mix.

requirements.title: Rendered audiovisual synchronization verification
requirements.statement: Synchronization acceptance shall measure the exported media, not only the internal offset calculation.

acceptance_criteria.text: A fixture with known visible events and audible impulses is decoded after export and checked at beginning, middle, and end.
The qualified test bound is at most one output video frame after accounting for container timestamps and audio encoder delay.
Conversion between 44.1 kHz and 48 kHz and between fractional and integer video rates does not silently change real-time duration.
Unverifiable real-world alignment remains labeled unverified or manual; the UI does not claim perfect lip synchronization without evidence.

requirements.title: Timed text and image overlays
requirements.statement: Users and AI shall add, edit, remove, and time text and image overlays through the same project editing model.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each overlay has explicit start and end, position, size, z-order, opacity, and applicable style settings.
A fixture overlay from 3 to 6 seconds appears at 3 seconds and disappears at 6 seconds under half-open interval semantics.
Image transparency, scaling, and text wrapping are represented in both preview and export.
Overlay edits are undoable and invalid timing or unknown image assets are rejected.

requirements.title: Contextual opening titles and end references
requirements.statement: The editor shall support brief opening titles, location/date labels, and ending references or credits without displaying them throughout the video by default.

acceptance_criteria.text: Initial suggestions use a configurable approximately 3-second opening title and 4-second ending card, bounded by the actual segment length.
Location and date wording comes from verified metadata or user labels; unknown locations are omitted or left for confirmation.
Users can choose project-level or section-level title placement and suppress repeated titles.
End references and credits accept user-supplied content and sources; the AI does not fabricate attribution.

requirements.title: Readable international text and safe areas
requirements.statement: Text overlays and captions shall support Unicode, configurable typography, readable contrast, and aspect-ratio-aware safe areas.

acceptance_criteria.text: Validate Latin and CJK sample strings with appropriately licensed font fallback and no missing-glyph boxes in reference renders.
Changing between 16:9, 1:1, and 9:16 exposes overflow and permits independent layout adjustments.
Text is passed to rendering libraries safely; punctuation and control-like strings do not become commands or filter expressions.
Font and text-style choices are persisted and exported with appropriate dependency or font-license documentation.

requirements.title: Basic overlay animation without tracking
requirements.statement: Overlays shall support simple timed opacity fades and explicit user-defined position or scale keyframes without following detected objects.

acceptance_criteria.text: Fade-in and fade-out durations can be edited and do not exceed the overlay duration without validation.
Keyframed values use defined interpolation and are identical in the composition contract for preview and rendering.
Static overlay operation does not depend on a tracking model.
No object- or motion-tracking implementation is introduced as a prerequisite for version one.

requirements.title: Editable date and location sections
requirements.statement: The project shall support named sections or chapters with explicit timeline boundaries, optionally suggested from recording days or locations.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can create, rename, move, split, and delete sections and correct automatic day/city groupings.
Suggestions record whether grouping derives from metadata, user labels, or uncertain inference.
Section boundaries remain valid after timeline edits using a documented anchoring policy.
A trip can contain multiple sections for one city or date; unknown metadata does not prevent manual organization.

requirements.title: Section and whole-project export
requirements.statement: Users shall export one section, selected sections, or the entire project through the same render pipeline.

acceptance_criteria.text: Individual section exports start at output time zero and correctly rebase overlays, audio, and subtitle cues.
Whole-project export preserves chosen section order and can include supported chapter metadata and a text chapter list.
Transitions crossing a section boundary have an explicit clip, include-handle, or rerender policy shown before export.
Batch section export reports independent job status and does not corrupt successful outputs if another section fails.

requirements.title: Non-destructive color and tonal controls
requirements.statement: The editor shall expose non-destructive exposure, contrast, saturation, white balance or temperature/tint, shadows, highlights, and tonal adjustments.

acceptance_criteria.text: Controls operate on a defined working color representation, have bounded values, and can be reset or bypassed.
The selected clip or project look can be inspected before and after adjustment without changing source bytes.
The grading model is exposed through validated editing operations rather than arbitrary filter-string injection.
Known color-ramp fixtures produce the documented tonal change in reference rendering.

requirements.title: Reusable project, camera, and clip color profiles
requirements.statement: Users shall save reusable color profiles and apply them project-wide, by camera/perspective, or to individual clips.

acceptance_criteria.text: A project profile affects all applicable current clips and newly imported clips according to an explicit inheritance rule.
Camera-level and clip-level overrides have visible precedence and never accidentally apply the same input transform twice.
Profiles can be named, duplicated, imported, exported, previewed, and reset without altering originals.
A linked preset update has a documented effect; users can detach or freeze an individual clip look.

requirements.title: Input color interpretation and SDR normalization
requirements.statement: The system shall distinguish technical input color transforms from creative looks and provide a validated SDR output path.

acceptance_criteria.text: Inspect color primaries, transfer, matrix, range, and available bit-depth metadata, and allow user correction when tags are absent or wrong.
Do not assume a DJI recording is log or apply a camera-specific LUT without confirmed profile information.
Default output uses a documented SDR Rec.709 path; recognized HDR inputs require supported tone mapping or an explicit unsupported warning.
Unknown log/HDR material is not silently labeled color-accurate; optional LUT import validates format and records provenance.

requirements.title: Color consistency across outputs
requirements.statement: Project and camera looks shall remain consistent across full exports, section exports, shorts, and available CPU/GPU encoding paths.

acceptance_criteria.text: All outputs inherit the intended grade unless an explicit per-output override is set.
Color tags and pixel format in the encoded file match the selected output policy.
Reference tests compare color patches with documented lossy-codec tolerances and detect double transforms or full/limited-range errors.
Hardware encoding availability does not imply every grading filter executes on the GPU.

requirements.title: Natural-language editing interface
requirements.statement: The editor shall offer a project-aware text interface for initial editing instructions and subsequent modifications.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can reference selected clips, named sections, visible timeline items, or a scoped time range in a prompt.
Show planning, analysis, proposal, application, and failure/cancel states rather than one indefinite spinner.
A request such as shorten the last section and move its title is converted to inspectable editing operations.
Provider errors or missing credentials do not masquerade as completed AI edits, and manual editing remains available.

requirements.title: End-to-end AI first draft
requirements.statement: From a populated collection and a high-level brief, the AI shall produce a playable first-draft timeline, not merely editing advice.

acceptance_criteria.text: The workflow examines available metadata and analysis, proposes camera groups and synchronization, organizes sections, and selects coherent source intervals.
It assembles split-screen and full-width segments, routes reference audio, applies the chosen look, and adds bounded titles and requested captions.
It reports uncertain alignment, exclusions, missing metadata, and assumptions without presenting them as verified facts.
An initial empty-project draft may apply automatically as a reversible transaction; replacing an existing edit requires a diff or explicit scoped authorization.

requirements.title: Reviewable and atomic AI edit proposals
requirements.statement: AI outputs shall be validated structured edit proposals with a readable diff, dry run, scoped application, and undo.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can inspect affected clips, source ranges, layout changes, audio changes, captions, and estimated expensive operations before acceptance.
A transaction either applies completely against the expected revision or leaves the project unchanged.
Repeating an idempotent request does not duplicate clips, captions, or export jobs.
Clear-all, overwrite, media deletion, external uploads, and spending actions are not silently authorized by a general editing prompt.

requirements.title: Grounded editorial reasoning
requirements.statement: AI recommendations shall be grounded in identified assets, source intervals, transcripts, metadata, or explicitly labeled visual inference.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every suggested cut, title fact, highlight, or content summary references the relevant asset and source range or a user instruction.
Unsupported claims about location, people, dialogue, or events are omitted or labeled uncertain.
Media analysis is retrieved in bounded chunks rather than sending every original video into every model request.
Candidate scores describe editorial estimates, not guaranteed correctness, engagement, or virality.

requirements.title: One typed editing command service
requirements.statement: The UI, internal AI, and external integrations shall use one versioned, typed editing service with shared validation.

acceptance_criteria.text: Support project inspection, asset search, analysis requests, timeline reads, validated batch edits, synchronization, profiles, subtitles, sections, and render-job operations.
Use stable identifiers, schema validation, expected revisions, idempotency keys, and structured errors.
Do not expose arbitrary shell commands, arbitrary filesystem writes, or raw unvalidated FFmpeg filter graphs as editing operations.
Unit and contract tests demonstrate that equivalent UI and AI requests yield equivalent project state.

requirements.title: MCP editing interface and external agent clients
requirements.statement: Expose the supported editor operations through a standards-based MCP server so externally configured Claude Code and Codex clients can inspect and edit a project.

acceptance_criteria.text: Provide working tool discovery, validated tool calls, concise descriptions, structured results, and references to paginated project resources.
Provide a local stdio connection and, when remote access is enabled, an authenticated Streamable HTTP configuration using the supported protocol/SDK version.
Long-running analysis and export calls return job identifiers with status and cancellation operations instead of holding a tool call open indefinitely.
Document and test a read -> propose -> validate -> apply -> export workflow from an MCP client; distinguish protocol-level tests from a live Claude/Codex integration test.

requirements.title: Provider-neutral language-model adapters
requirements.statement: The runtime shall support configurable Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible endpoints through explicit provider capabilities rather than one hard-coded model.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users configure server-side credentials, endpoint, model ID, and capability settings; a bounded connection test reports actual support.
Handle differences in tool calling, structured output, vision, streaming, timeouts, and context limits instead of assuming all OpenAI-compatible servers behave identically.
Text-only models remain usable for transcript-grounded editing; absent capabilities are clearly disabled or routed to another selected provider.
Use an available account-configured model by default; do not depend on a model name or subscription entitlement that has not been verified.

requirements.title: Claude Agent runtime adapter
requirements.statement: Provide a first-class optional server-side Claude Agent integration using the currently supported Claude Agent SDK and a constrained editor tool surface.

acceptance_criteria.text: Treat Claude Code or Claude Agent as an agent runtime, not a model ID or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
The adapter can start or resume a scoped editing request, stream progress, return a proposal, and cancel using supported SDK mechanisms.
Credentials and product authentication use supported provider mechanisms; do not copy developer-session tokens or assume a Claude subscription authorizes an embedded application.
Without the required installation or credentials, expose an actionable unavailable state and retain external MCP and other provider paths; do not label a stub verified.

requirements.title: Codex runtime adapter
requirements.statement: Provide a first-class optional server-side Codex integration using the current supported SDK or app-server interface and the same constrained editing tools.

acceptance_criteria.text: The adapter starts or resumes an editing request, reports streamed progress and cancellation, and returns validated proposals.
It does not assume Codex is a raw language model or implement against a removed CLI command.
Authentication, process isolation, and writable workspace are explicitly configured and do not expose original media or unrelated files to general coding tools.
Contract fixtures and a documented credentialed live smoke test distinguish adapter implementation from externally verified operation.

requirements.title: Hugging Face model registry and downloads
requirements.statement: The application shall support explicitly selected, downloadable Hugging Face analysis models with a model registry and bounded resource handling.

acceptance_criteria.text: The registry records task, repository ID, pinned revision, license, supported languages/modalities, files, and selected execution profile.
Downloads are opt-in, show progress and estimated storage, resume safely, and respect an application-controlled cache.
Do not enable arbitrary repository code or trust_remote_code by default; additional executable code requires separate reviewed approval.
Cached models can run offline; insufficient RAM/VRAM or unsupported acceleration results in a fallback choice or clear unavailable status rather than an OOM loop.

requirements.title: AI budgets, retries, caching, and cancellation
requirements.statement: AI and media-analysis workflows shall have configurable budgets, bounded retries, caching, cancellation, and persistent stage state.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can bound duration, model calls, token or cost limits when available, and local concurrency; unknown costs remain labeled unknown.
Cache analysis by source checksum, model revision, prompt/schema version, language, and relevant settings; invalidate stale entries.
Retry transient failures with limits and backoff, but do not blindly repeat a mutating operation or an authorization failure.
Cancellation stops queued work and terminates or safely detaches active processing, preserving already accepted project edits.

requirements.title: Untrusted media and prompt-injection boundary
requirements.statement: Filenames, transcripts, subtitles, metadata, OCR text, and model-generated captions shall be treated as untrusted content rather than executable instructions.

acceptance_criteria.text: A clip containing text that requests deleting files or leaking credentials cannot override the editing policy.
Provider outputs are parsed against schemas and authorized operations before any project mutation.
User-authored instructions are distinguished from quoted content inside media and retrieved analysis.
Prompt-injection regression fixtures are included for transcripts, filenames, and MCP tool results.

requirements.title: Tool authorization and credential boundaries
requirements.statement: Tool access shall be scoped by project and operation, with secrets held outside browser-visible data and project bundles.

acceptance_criteria.text: Read, edit, render, external-analysis, and administrative capabilities are separable; project A credentials cannot edit project B.
Remote MCP/API access is authenticated and follows a documented transport-security deployment profile.
Configurable local model endpoints are supported through explicit allowlists; arbitrary media URLs cannot become an SSRF route to private services.
Application logs, exported projects, AI context, error messages, and browser state do not contain raw secrets.

requirements.title: Speech extraction and local transcription
requirements.statement: Extract speech-bearing audio for automatic transcription with source-aligned timestamps and a functional CPU-capable local model path.

acceptance_criteria.text: Transcribe the selected audible source or explicit analysis source, retaining asset identity and source-time word or segment timestamps.
A multilingual small-model CPU profile is available; larger or GPU profiles are optional and resource-checked.
Silence and non-speech fixtures do not produce accepted invented dialogue; uncertain text is flagged and editable.
Transcription errors or unavailable models are visible and never replaced by fabricated transcript text.

requirements.title: Editable searchable source transcripts
requirements.statement: Users shall inspect, correct, and search transcripts linked to source intervals without changing original recordings.

acceptance_criteria.text: Search results jump to the relevant source or timeline occurrence and show asset identity.
Corrections preserve source timing or allow explicit timing adjustment and invalidate affected derived translations or summaries.
A source appearing multiple times on a timeline retains a single source transcript with separate timeline mappings.
Imported or manually written transcripts remain labeled as such, distinct from model-generated text.

requirements.title: Language detection and source-language control
requirements.statement: The transcription workflow shall support detected or user-selected source languages and preserve language metadata.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can override a wrong detected language per asset or transcript.
Original-language text is retained rather than silently replaced by a translation.
Mixed-language content is represented using the selected model capabilities and flagged where detection is uncertain.
The UI reports actual model-supported language capabilities rather than claiming every language is supported equally.

requirements.title: Translated subtitle language tracks
requirements.statement: The system shall generate editable translated subtitle tracks in user-selected target languages while preserving timing and original text.

acceptance_criteria.text: Translation is a distinct capability from speech recognition and may use the configured text provider or an explicitly installed translation model.
Preserve names and proper nouns where appropriate, keep source links, and mark translations as machine-generated until reviewed.
Changing a source cue marks affected translations stale without deleting user corrections silently.
When translation is unavailable, original-language captions still work and the missing capability is explained.

requirements.title: Toggleable single- and dual-language captions
requirements.statement: Users shall choose no captions, one language, or a primary plus secondary language in the editor without permanently burning them into source video.

acceptance_criteria.text: Caption visibility and selected language tracks can be changed during preview.
Dual-language display keeps the two languages distinguishable and avoids overlapping text.
Export settings independently choose sidecars, supported embedded tracks, or intentional burn-in.
Turning editor captions off does not delete the stored subtitle tracks or prohibit exporting sidecars.

requirements.title: Subtitle retiming through edits and synchronization
requirements.statement: Subtitle cues shall be derived from source-aligned text through the same time mappings used by video and audio.

acceptance_criteria.text: Trims, cuts, repeated source uses, synchronization offsets, drift correction, and section/short exports produce correct output cue timing.
Cues are split or clipped at removed regions rather than spanning unrelated footage.
No exported cue has negative duration, invalid ordering, or times beyond the selected output interval.
Editing a timeline does not corrupt the original source transcript timestamps.

requirements.title: Subtitle sidecars and supported embedded tracks
requirements.statement: Export per-language UTF-8 SRT and WebVTT subtitle files and offer compatible embedded subtitle tracks when the selected container supports them.

acceptance_criteria.text: One selected language produces a separately named, valid subtitle file with rebased output timing and language metadata.
Burn-in is optional and clearly distinguished from toggleable captions; original-language and translated files can be exported together.
Unsupported codec/container subtitle combinations are rejected or redirected to sidecars with an explanation.
Document uploading subtitle files to external platforms; do not claim that embedding tracks automatically creates selectable platform captions.

requirements.title: Caption formatting and manual cue editor
requirements.statement: Provide editable caption text, cue timings, line breaks, style, and readability checks suitable for different canvas ratios and languages.

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can correct text, split or merge cues, and adjust timings without regenerating the whole transcript.
Check safe-area overflow, excessive lines, and configurable reading-speed concerns without discarding speech automatically.
Title and primary/secondary caption regions can be adjusted to avoid collisions.
Caption styles remain consistent in authoritative preview and optional burn-in export.

requirements.title: Timestamped keyframes and shot summaries
requirements.statement: Create a bounded source index of representative timestamped frames, scene boundaries, metadata, and available transcript excerpts for AI retrieval.

acceptance_criteria.text: Extraction samples the whole source progressively with configurable limits instead of decoding every frame into memory.
Each frame or shot record includes asset ID, exact source interval, extraction method, and derived-asset provenance.
The AI can retrieve relevant subsets for an edit request and inspect where coverage is incomplete.
Basic metadata/transcript-driven drafting remains available when a visual model is not configured.

requirements.title: Optional local or remote visual-caption adapter
requirements.statement: Provide an optional visual-captioning adapter that can summarize selected frames or short windows using a configured vision model, including a documented Hugging Face candidate.

acceptance_criteria.text: At least one supported model execution path is implemented behind the adapter and has contract tests plus a reproducible live-model validation command.
Caption requests have frame-count, resolution, context, duration, and memory limits appropriate to detected hardware.
Results are timestamped visual inferences with provenance, not verified facts about identity, location, or unseen events.
When no feasible vision model is available, expose that limitation and use metadata/transcript evidence rather than returning placeholder visual descriptions.

requirements.title: Advanced continuous video understanding
requirements.statement: A later version may add richer continuous temporal video understanding and semantic retrieval beyond bounded frames, shots, and transcripts.

acceptance_criteria.text: Preserve extensible analysis schemas and source-time references in version one.
Do not require a large video model, vector database, tracking, or full-video semantic comprehension to ship version one.
Keep this feature visibly deferred and do not advertise it as implemented based on frame captions alone.

requirements.title: Grounded short-form highlight suggestions
requirements.statement: The AI shall propose short-form highlights with a default duration range of 15 to 20 seconds and editable editorial rationale.

acceptance_criteria.text: Default target is 18 seconds within the user-configurable 15..20-second range; source duration and hard constraints are respected.
Candidates reference selected source/project intervals, relevant transcript or visual evidence, and an explanation of the proposed hook or subject.
Prefer coherent starts and endings; if no adequate candidate exists, report that rather than padding with invented footage or claiming guaranteed engagement.
Users can compare candidates, choose one or several, and adjust their ranges before export.

requirements.title: Independent short sequences and reframing
requirements.statement: Shorts shall be derived editable sequences that reuse originals without destructively changing the main edit.

acceptance_criteria.text: Default short canvas is 1:1 as requested; 9:16, 16:9, and custom ratios remain selectable.
Derived shorts preserve intended sync, audio routing, grades, overlays, and subtitle time mappings.
Provide static split, stacked, full-width, or cropped composition options suitable for the chosen output; no tracking is required.
Editing a short does not mutate the parent sequence unless the user explicitly applies a supported shared change.

requirements.title: Short preview and batch delivery
requirements.statement: Users shall preview, adjust, and export selected short sequences with associated subtitles and publication metadata.

acceptance_criteria.text: Validate actual output duration, ratio, resolution, and audio after rendering; do not merely trust preset labels.
Provide per-short naming, thumbnail/reference frame, caption choices, and export job status.
Batch export isolates failures and uses bounded worker concurrency.
Platform presets are editable recommendations, dated when tied to external guidance, and not guarantees of platform acceptance.

requirements.title: Copyable SEO and publication suggestions
requirements.statement: The AI shall generate editable keyword, tag, title, and description suggestions for the whole video, a section, or a short.

acceptance_criteria.text: Suggestions are grounded in available content, locations, language, and user instructions, without invented claims.
Users can copy individual fields or export a text/JSON metadata bundle in a selected language.
Suggested keywords and hashtags are distinguished from technical container metadata and subtitle tracks.
The interface makes no promise of search ranking, reach, or virality and does not upload to a platform automatically.

requirements.title: Real export pipeline and default delivery profile
requirements.statement: The product shall render real playable video files from the composition graph, with an initial MP4/H.264/AAC SDR delivery profile and configurable output parameters.

acceptance_criteria.text: The initial delivery profile uses the project canvas/rate, normally 1920x1080 at resolved source-appropriate rate, with 48 kHz AAC audio.
Expose quality-based and target-bitrate controls with encoder-specific defaults; use a documented software starting point such as CRF 20 rather than claiming universal optimality.
Render video, selected audio, layouts, transforms, transitions, effects, and chosen captions; a downloaded project JSON is not a rendered video.
Outputs are written atomically and become downloadable only after validation succeeds.

requirements.title: Multiple containers and codec choices
requirements.statement: The editor shall offer validated export combinations beyond the default profile and show capability-dependent alternatives honestly.

acceptance_criteria.text: The reference software build supports MP4/H.264/AAC, WebM/VP9/Opus, and a documented MKV profile with correct muxing and playback tests.
Additional HEVC, AV1, ProRes/MOV, or other choices are exposed only when installed encoders and output constraints permit them.
The UI distinguishes container, video codec, audio codec, pixel format, quality, and bitrate.
Changing a container revalidates audio/subtitle compatibility rather than only changing the filename extension.

requirements.title: Mixed-rate input and controlled output timing
requirements.statement: Inputs with different frame rates shall play at their intended real-time speed within one configurable output rate.

acceptance_criteria.text: Validate combinations of 24, 25, 30, 60, 30000/1001, 60000/1001, and a variable-frame-rate fixture.
Default frame-rate conversion uses documented frame selection/repetition where necessary; optical-flow interpolation is not required.
Duration, audio timing, synchronization, and overlays remain aligned after conversion.
Exports record the exact rational output rate and do not relabel 59.94 material as 60 without an explicit conversion.

requirements.title: CPU-only reference rendering
requirements.statement: All version-one editing and mandatory export operations shall have a functional CPU-only rendering path.

acceptance_criteria.text: The application starts, imports, edits, and exports in the documented reference environment without a GPU.
The CPU renderer supports the same required composition semantics as accelerated profiles.
No visual analysis model or cloud provider is required merely to render an existing timeline.
Tests use real media and decoding of outputs; a mocked render job cannot satisfy this requirement.

requirements.title: Capability-tested hardware acceleration
requirements.statement: Detect and use available hardware acceleration for supported processing stages, with explicit CPU fallback and truthful capability reporting.

acceptance_criteria.text: Probe compiled encoders, device access, and a short real encode before declaring a GPU path usable; an encoder name alone is insufficient.
Provide an NVIDIA NVENC acceleration profile when available on the reference Linux deployment; other hardware backends may be added through the same capability layer.
Report acceleration separately for decode, filters/composition, encode, and AI inference.
If acceleration fails, offer or perform the configured CPU retry without changing project content; report which path actually produced the output.
GPU integration tests are conditional on real hardware and reported as not run when unavailable, never as CPU-tested GPU success.

requirements.title: Durable asynchronous jobs
requirements.statement: Import analysis, proxies, AI drafts, and exports shall run as durable jobs with observable state, bounded concurrency, cancellation, and safe retry.

acceptance_criteria.text: Jobs have queued, running, succeeded, failed, and cancelled states, input revision, progress, timestamps, and structured failure details.
A process crash recovers queued work and marks interrupted work for safe restart; partially written outputs are not published.
Retrying a job with the same idempotency key does not duplicate an accepted project transaction or completed output.
Long jobs run outside HTTP request handlers and preserve a responsive application; resource limits prevent unbounded parallel encoders/models.

requirements.title: Export preflight and decoded-output validation
requirements.statement: Preflight exports and verify the produced files against the selected immutable revision and output contract.

acceptance_criteria.text: Before rendering, validate source availability, intervals, capabilities, free disk space, audio routing, font availability, and relevant subtitle choices.
After rendering, probe dimensions, exact rate, streams, codecs, duration, color metadata, and decode representative or complete small-test outputs.
Check reference frames and audio for critical fixtures, detecting black outputs, missing overlays, doubled audio, or truncated endings.
Validation failure leaves the job failed with diagnostics and never presents an invalid file as a completed delivery.

requirements.title: Editable output presets and quality guidance
requirements.statement: Offer sensible editable export presets, with visible tradeoffs between dimensions, rate, quality, bitrate, speed, and estimated file size.

acceptance_criteria.text: Provide landscape 16:9, square 1:1, and portrait 9:16 starting profiles using the selected content and platform-independent defaults.
Preserve the user-selected output ratio and rate when recommending bitrate or encoder choices.
Label size and time estimates as estimates, and warn about avoidable upscaling or unsupported combinations.
Encoder-specific controls are mapped explicitly; do not assume software CRF and hardware quality numbers have identical meaning.

requirements.title: Storage quotas and safe derived-file cleanup
requirements.statement: The application shall manage derived media storage with quotas, preflight checks, safe temporary directories, and recoverable cleanup.

acceptance_criteria.text: Low disk space prevents unsafe work or cancels it with a clear error while preserving originals and durable edits.
Cache cleanup removes only identified unreferenced derived files within application-owned roots.
Failed or cancelled jobs clean temporary outputs without deleting unrelated files or other jobs artifacts.
Users can inspect media, proxy, model-cache, and render storage separately.

requirements.title: Complete output delivery bundle
requirements.statement: Deliver a coherent output bundle containing the rendered video and the selected supporting artifacts.

acceptance_criteria.text: Bundle selected per-language captions, chapter list, editable publication metadata, and a render manifest with source/project revision and output settings.
Artifacts use consistent names and match the same exported time range.
No credentials, private filesystem paths, or unintended GPS data leak into publication bundles.
Users can download an individual artifact or the complete bundle.

requirements.title: Self-hostable browser application and CPU reference setup
requirements.statement: Deliver a working desktop-browser editor backed by a local or self-hosted media-processing service, with a documented CPU-first reference deployment.

acceptance_criteria.text: Provide repeatable installation/start commands, persistent storage configuration, migrations, and health checks.
A reference Linux environment can run without Docker when cloud-development policy prevents nested containers; container deployment is also documented.
Do not depend on Claude Code Cloud as a permanent production host, storage service, or GPU provider.
Bind local-only deployments safely by default; remote exposure requires the documented authentication and transport settings.

requirements.title: Real-media automated verification suite
requirements.statement: Implement layered automated verification with real generated media fixtures, independent expected outcomes, and traceability to acceptance criteria.

acceptance_criteria.text: Include unit tests for time mappings, contract tests for editing tools, integration tests using the real renderer, and browser end-to-end journeys.
Generate small fixtures with known timestamps, event markers, audio impulses, aspect ratios, and rate/offset/drift variations.
At least one regression exercises approximately 2K input at 60 fps and validates actual output content and synchronization.
Mocks are limited to provider/network isolation and cannot alone satisfy media, AI quality, or hardware integration claims.

requirements.title: Measured responsiveness and bounded memory
requirements.statement: Keep interactive editing responsive and media processing memory-bounded, with declared reference hardware and measurable performance tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: On the declared reference browser/system, a 300-item timeline targets p95 under 150 ms for local selection/trim feedback after assets are indexed, excluding network and rendering completion.
Exercise two 2560x1440 60 fps sources in a CPU render smoke test; record elapsed time and peak memory instead of promising real-time export.
On the reference 4-vCPU/8-GiB CPU worker profile, one baseline render job excluding optional local LLM/VLM inference stays within a configured 6-GiB worker budget.
Import large files and analyze long recordings with streaming/chunked processing; do not read an entire recording into application RAM.
If a target cannot be met, report the benchmark and bottleneck; do not silently lower input rate, resolution, or test coverage.

requirements.title: Observable jobs and reproducible diagnostics
requirements.statement: Provide structured diagnostics that identify the state and provenance of media and AI processing without exposing secrets.

acceptance_criteria.text: Record job ID, project revision, relevant asset IDs, engine/model versions, settings, actual device path, and redacted errors.
Users can inspect progress and export a redacted diagnostic report.
Log noisy media-process output in bounded files rather than filling the UI or agent context.
An exported manifest identifies enough configuration to reproduce a rendering decision on compatible software.

requirements.title: Safe media processing boundary
requirements.statement: Process uploaded media and images as untrusted input with constrained subprocesses, paths, protocols, and resource usage.

acceptance_criteria.text: Build subprocess argument arrays without shell interpolation; validate or safely serialize any generated filter expressions.
Prevent path traversal, symlink escape, decompression/resource abuse, unapproved protocols, and unauthorized network fetches.
Use supported patched dependencies, per-job working directories, timeouts, cancellation, and least-privilege workers.
Security tests cover malicious filenames, overlay text, project bundles, subtitles, and oversized or malformed media.

requirements.title: Private-by-default media and secrets handling
requirements.statement: Keep original recordings, location metadata, transcripts, and credentials private by default and require clear configuration before external processing.

acceptance_criteria.text: Local import, manual editing, and CPU export do not upload source media to model providers.
Before enabling remote analysis, show which data types and approximate payloads leave the system and allow text-only or reduced-frame policies.
Secrets are server-side and redacted; they are excluded from repositories, browser responses, project exports, prompts, and logs.
Provide retention and deletion controls for derived analysis without deleting originals by default.

requirements.title: Pinned dependencies and license inventory
requirements.statement: Deliver reproducible dependency configuration and a documented inventory of software, model, codec, and font licensing considerations.

acceptance_criteria.text: Pin supported stable dependency versions and model revisions in lockfiles or equivalent reproducible manifests.
Use permissively usable defaults where feasible; do not introduce paid SDKs or subscription-gated editing components without approval.
Document the actual FFmpeg build and enabled codecs rather than claiming all possible codec distributions have identical licensing.
Provide dependency-update and vulnerability-check commands and report unresolved issues honestly.

requirements.title: Accessible, discoverable editing interface
requirements.statement: Deliver a usable desktop editing layout with a collection, preview, timeline, inspector, AI panel, and job/output views.

acceptance_criteria.text: Core actions have labels, keyboard access, focus visibility, useful empty states, and actionable errors.
Provide numeric alternatives to pointer-only trim, crop, synchronization, and overlay-position controls.
Test current Chromium and Firefox desktop paths supported by the chosen proxy formats and document any browser limitations.
Editing and export remain available when AI analysis is busy or disabled; no dead primary buttons or decorative-only timeline.

requirements.title: Crash recovery and safe migrations
requirements.statement: Project persistence and schema migrations shall recover safely from crashes and preserve existing user edits.

acceptance_criteria.text: Transactions interrupted before commit leave the previous revision intact; interrupted jobs can be inspected and retried.
Back up or otherwise safely checkpoint project data before destructive schema migration.
Version checks reject unsupported states instead of guessing at missing fields.
Recovery tests restart the application during autosave, analysis, and export and verify originals and accepted edits remain intact.

requirements.title: Offline editing and graceful AI degradation
requirements.statement: Once installed, manual editing and supported CPU export shall work without an external model connection, and cached local analysis shall work where its dependencies are present.

acceptance_criteria.text: Disconnected operation still permits project load, preview, manual edits, and render to supported local formats.
Cached speech models operate offline; missing uncached models produce a clear download requirement.
A deterministic metadata-based draft may be offered but is explicitly labeled rule-based and does not count as a successful generative-AI integration.
Provider or model failures preserve accepted project state and leave alternative manual workflows usable.

requirements.title: User and developer handover
requirements.statement: Deliver complete instructions for operating, extending, testing, and deploying the implemented editor.

acceptance_criteria.text: Include a quick start, example split/full/split project, provider setup, CPU/GPU configuration, subtitle/section/short export, and recovery guide.
Document the project schema, typed editing API, MCP setup, model registry, renderer assumptions, and known limitations.
Provide screenshots or a recorded walkthrough from the actual running application and generated test media, not a mock design.
List exact verified commands and distinguish tested features from implemented but externally unverified integrations.

requirements.title: Adopt and preserve the supplied requirements baseline
requirements.statement: The implementing agent shall integrate this specification into the existing bootstrapped repository without re-running or replacing the bootstrap.

acceptance_criteria.text: Preserve this input package as an immutable baseline and map every AVE-REQ ID to its canonical working requirement file.
Populate the existing PRODUCT, ARCHITECTURE, ROADMAP, PROGRESS, ASSUMPTIONS, and TRACEABILITY documents without losing meaningful existing content.
Explicit user requirements and exclusions cannot be demoted or rewritten merely to fit an easier implementation.
Requirement implementation status starts unverified; package validation is not product verification.

requirements.title: Capability-aware native dynamic workflows
requirements.statement: Claude Code shall use task-specific native dynamic workflows where actually available, with a documented bounded fallback to subagents or sequential execution.

acceptance_criteria.text: Probe the current environment for workflow tools, available models, subagents, worktree isolation, permissions, hooks, network, browser tools, CPU/RAM, and accelerator access.
When native workflows are available, compose requirement-specific investigation, implementation, testing, and independent review with structured handoffs and dependency-aware parallelism.
Validate native workflow syntax against the installed runtime; do not invent APIs or assume a published feature is enabled in this cloud session.
When unavailable, perform the same lifecycle through bounded subagent/sequential tasks; do not build a custom orchestration platform instead of the editor.

requirements.title: Evidence-driven workflow self-improvement
requirements.statement: The coding workflow shall improve its repository-local procedures based on observed failures and measured outcomes, without weakening product or verification constraints.

acceptance_criteria.text: Record repeated failure, proposed improvement, affected workflow, measurement, and rollback plan in a concise workflow log.
Apply small reviewed changes to skills, task decomposition, context retrieval, or test scheduling and verify them against fixed regression fixtures.
Do not loosen acceptance criteria, skip tests, raise tolerances, remove security gates, or rewrite expected results to make an implementation pass.
Keep improvements only when they show useful evidence; avoid permanent agent proliferation and recurring harness rewrites.

requirements.title: Isolated bounded tasks and independent review
requirements.statement: Delegate bounded tasks with explicit context and deliverables, using verified worktree isolation for concurrent writers and a fresh review context for acceptance.

acceptance_criteria.text: Task briefs include requirement IDs, acceptance criteria, allowed paths, dependencies, input revision, test commands, and handback schema.
Initialize isolated tasks from the intended integration commit; do not assume the native worktree default matches the current branch.
A reviewer receives requirements and the diff rather than relying on the implementer claim of success; media-critical tests inspect real rendered outputs.
Respect actual concurrency and resource limits; never recursively multiply coding agents or bypass a cloud limit.

requirements.title: Verification gates that cannot pass as placeholders
requirements.statement: Replace bootstrap-only verification with staged real checks and independently verifiable release gates as implementation begins.

acceptance_criteria.text: Keep a fast feedback tier, real-media integration tier, and full release tier behind documented repository commands.
Tie verification evidence to a commit/tree fingerprint, configuration, requirement IDs, and test results; stale evidence cannot certify changed code.
Use supported hooks only after a small smoke test; avoid recursive Stop-hook loops and repeated full renders on every conversational response.
No-op scripts, skipped integration tests, caught exceptions returning success, or provider mocks cannot establish completed product requirements.

requirements.title: Persistent progress and bounded autonomous continuation
requirements.statement: Claude Code shall persist actionable progress and continue unblocked work within actual session limits, then leave an exact resumable state.

acceptance_criteria.text: Update the current objective, requirement statuses, blockers, failed checks, changed files, and next command after coherent work units.
Reconstruct state from repository files and Git after compaction or a new session rather than relying on conversational memory.
At a genuine permission, resource, credential, or session limit, preserve partial results and report the exact unblock action without claiming ongoing execution.
Do not use infinite loops, arbitrary sleep daemons, or permission bypass flags to simulate unlimited autonomy.

requirements.title: Honest completion and conditional verification
requirements.statement: Requirements shall be marked complete only with applicable acceptance evidence; missing external resources shall remain visible verification gaps.

acceptance_criteria.text: Distinguish planned, in progress, implemented, verified, blocked, and deferred states in the working project tracker.
A real credentialed provider smoke test is required to claim that provider path verified; an actual device encode is required to claim a hardware path verified.
Absence of optional hardware can yield a documented conditional capability, not a claim that it was tested or a silent scope reduction.
Release reporting enumerates all remaining unverified criteria and never describes a mock interface or partial milestone as the whole requested product.

requirements.title: Milestone-level product validation
requirements.statement: At every meaningful milestone, compare the running product with the original brief and the complete version-one requirement set.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run integrated import -> draft -> manual/AI revision -> mixed-layout preview -> section/short/full export journeys.
Check that synchronization, final audio, captions, color profiles, and metadata still agree after integration.
Do not stop at the first playable MVP or a backend-only renderer while remaining version-one requirements are unimplemented.
Keep future tracking and advanced temporal understanding excluded; further scope additions require an explicit rationale and must not displace requested work.

requirements.title: Object and motion tracking
requirements.statement: A future release may add motion/object tracking and automatically moving overlays or crops; version one explicitly excludes these capabilities.

acceptance_criteria.text: Version one supports static crop/position controls and manual keyframes without a tracking dependency.
No tracking models, moving-object identity system, or subject-following feature is required for any version-one acceptance gate.
Keep this capability in the future roadmap and do not claim it is implemented by static keyframe extraction or shared-event synchronization.
